episodes.201064: Higher moisture moved into eastern New Mexico early on May 25th behind a backdoor cold front. This added moisture combined with lift ahead of a weakening upper low over Utah resulting in the development of scattered showers and storms along and east of the central mountain chain. Several of these storms became strong to severe with one producing quarter size hail near Tierra Monte in the east slopes of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains and another producing a tornado near Floyd in western Roosevelt County and quarter to ping pong ball size hail between Cannon Air Force Base and downtown Clovis. Storms across eastern New Mexico mostly tapered off around sunset while the convectively enhanced backdoor front pushed west through the gaps of the central mountain chain. ||Key Words: Severe Thunderstorm Winds, Large Hail, Tornado, Funnel Cloud.||Another round of showers and storms developed and moved across north central and eastern New Mexico during the afternoon and evening hours of May 26th due to higher surface moisture in place combining with added lift and instability from the upper level disturbance moving overhead. Penny to golf ball size hail was observed at several locations, a brief tornado was observed near Montezuma northeast of Las Vegas, and damaging straight line winds resulted in a flipped and overturned an 18-wheeler trailer near Forrest in southern Quay County. Storms exited east into Texas around sunset.
episodes.201142: Low pressure located over the Dakotas was slowly moving eastward across the Upper-Mississippi River Valley. Isolated to scattered rain showers developed diurnally, which a few cells across western Minnesota had enough instability ( 100 to 300 J/kg of MuCAPE) to produce heavier rain and a few rumbles of thunder. Given this region of Minnesota was within close proximity of the closed low combined with weak instability, funnel clouds could not be ruled out. ||About five miles southeast of Sleepy Eye, MN a few trained spotters noticed one cell in particular produced a funnel cloud that moved northwest for approximately ten minutes. Spotters confirmed the funnel never reached the ground.
episodes.201189: Several afternoons of thunderstorm activity occurred during the fourth week of May, with hail and wind damage being reported around Central Alabama over the course of four days. In addition, heavy rainfall on May 27 resulted in several impassable roadways along Terrapin Creek in Cherokee County.
episodes.201209: Scattered thunderstorms developed across Middle Tennessee during the afternoon and evening of May 27, 2025. While these thunderstorms were non-severe, gusty winds from a thunderstorm in Grundy County downed a few trees.
episodes.201222: Strong to severe thunderstorms, including miniature supercells, developed during the late afternoon and early evening hours before weakening and pushing east into Georgia after midnight. The thunderstorms produced damaging winds and a tornado in north central portions of Alabama. Isolated flash flooding occurred as well.
episodes.201247: A line of showers and thunderstorms ahead of a surface trough stretch into southeast Alabama and brought a few reports of trees down.
episodes.201269: The large-scale weather pattern featured a split flow with a southern jet stream stretching from northern Mexico into the Gulf States. A weak upper-level disturbance, near the Baja Peninsula, moved into the Big Bend region by evening. Ahead of this feature, southeasterly winds helped push deeper moisture into far West Texas, aided by earlier storms. With strong surface heating in place west of this moisture, isolated thunderstorms developed by late afternoon across higher terrain in West Texas and northeastern Mexico. Later in the night, a strengthening low-level jet organized some of these storms into larger clusters, leading to damaging winds.
episodes.201270: The large-scale weather pattern featured a split flow with a southern jet stream stretching from northern Mexico into the Gulf States. A weak upper-level disturbance, near the Baja Peninsula, moved into the Big Bend region by evening. Ahead of this feature, southeasterly winds helped push deeper moisture into far West Texas, aided by earlier storms. With strong surface heating in place west of this moisture, isolated thunderstorms developed by late afternoon across higher terrain in West Texas and northeastern Mexico. Later in the night, a strengthening low-level jet organized some of these storms into larger clusters, leading to elevated winds.
episodes.201542: A thunderstorm produce one inch hail and a tornado that skipped across the ground over an open field. Dust was lofted into the air at times. The tornado hit a farm. Out of 9 buildings on their property, only one (an old garage) was hit and destroyed. It lifted the roof off the old garage, then the walls collapsed.
episodes.201878: Isolated severe thunderstorms developed in eastern New Mexico on the afternoon of the 26th and moved into West Texas late in the evening. Lower level atmospheric flow became more northeasterly this day leading to cooler temperatures and less surface based instability than observed in previous days. This upslope flow regime promoted the development of thunderstorms in eastern New Mexico and then propagated into West Texas late in the evening. A few of these storms became severe with abundant elevated instability still present. One severe storm moved across northern Hall County producing golf ball size hail. A second severe storm moved across Yoakum County producing wind damage and then golf ball size hail once it moved into Terry County.
episodes.202084: Thunderstorms produced damaging winds across portions of southeast Texas.
episodes.202171: An upper-level shortwave trough moved across a cold front over South-Central Texas and generated thunderstorms. The warm, moist airmass had steep mid-level lapse rates, and some of the storms produced large hail. There were also a few reports of damaging wind gusts and heavy rain that led to flash flooding.
episodes.202268: Continuing the pattern from May 24th and 25th, an incoming trough (with embedded disturbances) interacted with a dryline and produced isolated storms in the eastern Permian Basin of West Texas. One thunderstorm developed in Glasscock County and produced hail up to 2 inches in diameter south of Garden City before it moved east of the Midland/Odessa CWA. An additional thunderstorm moved into northern Lea County later in the evening and produced a 58 mph wind gust.
episodes.202273: A trough passing over the region, a nearby dryline, and upslope surface flow allowed for the development of scattered thunderstorms across Southeast New Mexico and West Texas. Large hail was reported in Brewster County in/near the higher elevation. Some strong winds were also measured that evening. High non-thunderstorm winds were also reported in the Guadalupe Mountains overnight as the trough/Pacific front moved through.
episodes.202440: A late-evening round of severe weather occurred across northwestern into west-central Oklahoma on the 26th. Thunderstorm activity was focused near and beneath an upper low aloft (i.e., cold temperatures), promoting a sufficient overlap of instability and lapse rates for large to very large hail.
episodes.202531: A thunderstorm moving offshore produced strong wind gusts at Cape Canaveral.
episodes.202532: Multiple reports received of funnel clouds along the I-4 corridor due to thunderstorms along the sea breeze collision.
episodes.202606: Widespread thunderstorms developed in east Texas on May 26th along a stalled frontal boundary. Those storms merged into a Mesoscale Convective System late in the afternoon and raced southeastward. As those storms moved across the local area, a severe wind gust was produced in the local marine area.
episodes.202607: Widespread thunderstorms developed in east Texas on May 26th along a stalled frontal boundary. Those storms merged into a Mesoscale Convective System late in the afternoon and raced southeastward. As those storms moved across the local area, a severe wind gust wind gust occurred in Pointe Coupee Parish.
episodes.202825: A cold front moved across central Georgia, interacting with the southern edge of the CAD wedge in the afternoon hours of the 27th. Storms near the intersection of the front and the wedge latched on to the resultant shear and generated several tornados in Carrol and Coweta counties.
episodes.202991: Scattered to numerous thunderstorms developed along a subtle stationary boundary in the late afternoon and early evening hours across portions of southeast Georgia. A few of these storms became strong enough to produce damaging wind gusts.
episodes.203065: Severe weather accompanied a complex of thunderstorms as it surged southeast through Oklahoma into North Texas the night of May 25, with damaging winds being the prevalent severe event. Thunderstorms subsided the morning of May 26, then redeveloped that afternoon along the remnant outflow boundary and attendant surface front. Both large hail and damaging winds occurred as the afternoon storms pushed south through Central Texas, eventually exiting the area to the south that evening.
episodes.203097: During the afternoon of the 26th several isolated supercells formed in the eastern Texas Panhandle and some produced hail up to the size of tennis balls. After these storms moved east of the Panhandle, a storm complex moved into the southwestern Texas Panhandle from New Mexico. This complex produced hail up to half dollar size along with severe wind gusts up to 68 mph.
episodes.203188: A lightning strike caused a fire, which destroyed a home in Sanford.
episodes.203275: A dissipating front combined with upper-level energy to produce two lines of thunderstorms on successive mornings in late May 2025. The first situation, a decaying line of broken showers and a few thunderstorms, raced southward across the Lower Texas Gulf/Laguna Madre waters during the early morning of the 27th. On May 28th, a more intense squall line developed inland and gradually moved into the nearshore Gulf waters.  Gale-force wind gusts and torrential rainfall accompanied the second line in a few locations along the coast.

Pencil-thin tornado touched down in southern Weld County then slowly moved south across the county line into Morgan County. Several reports of the tornado were received from the fire department and storm chasers/spotter, and it was hard to discern ground contact through the entire path though one funnel was observed throughout the event. The tornado struck an old garage on a farm property just east of County Road 15 in extreme northern Morgan County. The tornado lifted the roof off the garage, which caused the walls to collapse. No other structures on the property were damaged. The owner was on-site during the tornado and mentioned how narrow the tornado was, and that it lifted not long after hitting the old garage.

A brief tornado touched down on Redstone Arsenal just off Ranger Road. The tornado bent fencing while entering the property, then proceeded to shift dozens of 500 lb. storage tanks, tossing about 3 of them. Another metal trough tank was also tipped over and tossed. Then, after plowing through a chain-link fence, the tornado struck a light metal frame storage building. The bolts connecting the support columns to the foundation slab were sheared on three of the columns. The entire western flank of the building was collapsed in by the tornado, with metal framework bent as well. Some of the contents of the building were tossed out and strewn downwind several hundred yards found by on-site employees. As quickly as the tornado developed, it dissipated short of Saturn Drive, with no further identifiable damage found downwind.
